claim: Diverse cellular signaling events, including B cell receptor (BCR) activation, are hypothesized to be facilitated by domains enriched in specific plasma membrane lipids and proteins that resemble liquid-ordered phase-separated domains in model membranes.
source: Diverse cellular signaling events, including B cell receptor (BCR) activation, are hypothesized to be facilitated by domains enriched in specific plasma membrane lipids and proteins that resemble liquid-ordered phase-separated domains in model membranes.
evidence: This is a statement about existing hypotheses in the field, supported by citations throughout the introduction section.

claim: The concept of lipid raft domains remains controversial and lacks direct experimental support in intact cells.
source: This concept remains controversial and lacks direct experimental support in intact cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, supported by citations in the introduction discussing limitations of prior methods.

claim: Super-resolution fluorescence localization microscopy can visualize ordered and disordered domains in mouse B lymphoma cell membranes.
source: Here, we visualize ordered and disordered domains in mouse B lymphoma cell membranes using super-resolution fluorescence localization microscopy
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in Figures 1 and 2, showing direct visualization of domains.

claim: Clustered BCR resides within ordered phase-like domains capable of sorting key regulators of BCR activation.
source: demonstrate that clustered BCR resides within ordered phase-like domains capable of sorting key regulators of BCR activation
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 2 and 3 showing co-localization of BCR with ordered domain markers and sorting of regulatory proteins.

claim: Clustering receptors leads to their collective activation by stabilizing an extended ordered domain.
source: present a minimal, predictive model where clustering receptors leads to their collective activation by stabilizing an extended ordered domain
evidence: This is supported by the computational model presented in Figure 4 and experimental validation in Figure 5.

claim: Lipid mediated forces can bias biochemical networks in ways that broadly impact signal transduction.
source: Overall, these studies demonstrate that lipid mediated forces can bias biochemical networks in ways that broadly impact signal transduction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental and modeling results presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: PM peptide partitions into ordered domains in GPMVs.
source: Probe partitioning was verified in isolated giant plasma membrane vesicles (GPMVs) imaged at low temperature as demonstrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.
evidence: This is directly demonstrated by the GPMV imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: TM peptide partitions into disordered domains in GPMVs.
source: YFP-TM and Alexa647 CTxB partition into alternate phases, indicating that TM partitions into the liquid-disordered phase.
evidence: This is demonstrated by GPMV imaging data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2d.

claim: GG peptide partitions into disordered domains in GPMVs.
source: eGFP-GG and Alexa647 CTxB partition into alternate phases, indicating that GG partitions into the liquid-disordered phase.
evidence: This is demonstrated by GPMV imaging data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2c.

claim: TM clusters are enriched in GG peptide compared to the membrane as a whole.
source: Pair cross-correlation functions indicate that TM clusters are enriched in GG and depleted of PM on average compared to the membrane as a whole (Figure 1c, left panel), consistent with the partitioning of these probes into disordered domains in GPMVs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation analysis shown in Figure 1c.

claim: TM clusters are depleted of PM peptide compared to the membrane as a whole.
source: Pair cross-correlation functions indicate that TM clusters are enriched in GG and depleted of PM on average compared to the membrane as a whole (Figure 1c, left panel), consistent with the partitioning of these probes into disordered domains in GPMVs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation analysis shown in Figure 1c.

claim: CTxB clusters are enriched in PM peptide.
source: Pair cross-correlation functions indicate that PM is enriched and TM is depleted on average within CTxB clusters (Figure 1c, right panel), in good agreement with the partitioning of these probes into ordered domains in GPMVs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation analysis shown in Figure 1c.

claim: CTxB clusters are depleted of TM peptide.
source: Pair cross-correlation functions indicate that PM is enriched and TM is depleted on average within CTxB clusters (Figure 1c, right panel), in good agreement with the partitioning of these probes into ordered domains in GPMVs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation analysis shown in Figure 1c.

claim: At most 20% enrichment or depletion of peptide probes within clustered protein domains was observed.
source: The spatial heterogeneity observed within TM or CTxB clusters is subtle; we observed at most 20% enrichment or depletion of the peptide probes within the clustered protein domains
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the cross-correlation data in Figure 1.

claim: The observed enrichment or depletion is an underestimate of the actual enrichment or depletion due to the finite lateral resolution of the measurement.
source: although this is an underestimate of the actual enrichment or depletion due to the finite lateral resolution of the measurement (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulations in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 showing how finite resolution reduces observed correlation magnitudes.

claim: TM clusters (68 nm) were on average larger than CTxB clusters (40 nm).
source: Relevant to this point, we found that TM clusters (68 nm) were on average larger than CTxB clusters (40 nm), which were on the order of our cumulative resolution (40 nm) in the measurements summarized in Figure 1c.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the imaging data.

claim: The cumulative resolution in the measurements was approximately 40 nm.
source: which were on the order of our cumulative resolution (40 nm) in the measurements summarized in Figure 1c.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the imaging system.

claim: The weaker enrichment and depletion of lipid probes within CTxB clusters compared to TM clusters may be due to the limited resolution of these measurements.
source: It is possible that the weaker enrichment and depletion of lipid probes within CTxB clusters as compared to TM clusters is simply due to the limited resolution of these measurements.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the relationship between cluster size and measurement resolution.

claim: Error in cross-correlation measurements was dominated by probe sampling statistics.
source: Error in these measurements was dominated by probe sampling statistics (Figure 1—figure supplement 5) because the surface density of probes (2–20 μm−2) is such that only a few peptides co-localize with nanosized clustered protein domains within an image of a single chemically fixed cell.
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 5 comparing different sources of error.

claim: The surface density of probes was 2–20 μm−2.
source: because the surface density of probes (2–20 μm−2) is such that only a few peptides co-localize with nanosized clustered protein domains within an image of a single chemically fixed cell.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the imaging data.

claim: Clustered plasma membrane proteins can stabilize domains spanning both plasma membrane leaflets that sort established markers of ordered and disordered domains in intact cell membranes.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that clustered plasma membrane proteins can stabilize domains spanning both plasma membrane leaflets that sort established markers of ordered and disordered domains in intact cell membranes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: Depletion of markers from domains of the alternate phase is a property of liquid-ordered and liquid-disordered domains in phase separated membranes.
source: Importantly, we observe depletion of markers from domains of the alternate phase, as well as equivalency between order-and disorder-driven sorting. These are properties of liquid-ordered and liquid-disordered domains in phase separated membranes (Veatch and Keller, 2005); therefore we refer to them as phase-like domains.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work on model membrane systems.

claim: PM peptide was enriched in BCR clusters in chemically fixed CH27 B cells.
source: The sorting of phase sensitive peptides with respect to BCR clusters was observed in chemically fixed CH27 B cells (Figure 2a), live CH27 B cells (Figure 2b), and chemically fixed primary mouse B cells (Figure 2c). In all cases we found that the PM peptide was enriched and the TM peptide was excluded from BCR clusters.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 2a.

claim: TM peptide was excluded from BCR clusters in chemically fixed CH27 B cells.
source: The sorting of phase sensitive peptides with respect to BCR clusters was observed in chemically fixed CH27 B cells (Figure 2a), live CH27 B cells (Figure 2b), and chemically fixed primary mouse B cells (Figure 2c). In all cases we found that the PM peptide was enriched and the TM peptide was excluded from BCR clusters.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 2a.

claim: PM peptide was enriched in BCR clusters in live CH27 B cells.
source: The sorting of phase sensitive peptides with respect to BCR clusters was observed in chemically fixed CH27 B cells (Figure 2a), live CH27 B cells (Figure 2b), and chemically fixed primary mouse B cells (Figure 2c). In all cases we found that the PM peptide was enriched and the TM peptide was excluded from BCR clusters.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 2b.

claim: TM peptide was excluded from BCR clusters in live CH27 B cells.
source: The sorting of phase sensitive peptides with respect to BCR clusters was observed in chemically fixed CH27 B cells (Figure 2a), live CH27 B cells (Figure 2b), and chemically fixed primary mouse B cells (Figure 2c). In all cases we found that the PM peptide was enriched and the TM peptide was excluded from BCR clusters.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 2b.

claim: PM peptide was enriched in BCR clusters in chemically fixed primary mouse B cells.
source: The sorting of phase sensitive peptides with respect to BCR clusters was observed in chemically fixed CH27 B cells (Figure 2a), live CH27 B cells (Figure 2b), and chemically fixed primary mouse B cells (Figure 2c). In all cases we found that the PM peptide was enriched and the TM peptide was excluded from BCR clusters.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 2c.

claim: TM peptide was excluded from BCR clusters in chemically fixed primary mouse B cells.
source: The sorting of phase sensitive peptides with respect to BCR clusters was observed in chemically fixed CH27 B cells (Figure 2a), live CH27 B cells (Figure 2b), and chemically fixed primary mouse B cells (Figure 2c). In all cases we found that the PM peptide was enriched and the TM peptide was excluded from BCR clusters.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 2c.

claim: The direct measurements of peptide sorting are generally consistent with past FRET and biochemical isolation measurements that argued that clustered BCR resides within ordered membrane domains.
source: The direct measurements of peptide sorting shown here are generally consistent with past FRET and biochemical isolation measurements that argued that clustered BCR resides within ordered membrane domains (Cheng et al., 1999; Pierce, 2002; Sohn et al., 2006, 2008b).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior published work, supported by citations.

claim: The association between clustered BCR and the ordered domain marker PM appears more sustained in imaging measurements than was observed in past reports using FRET.
source: The association between clustered BCR and the ordered domain marker PM appears more sustained in our imaging measurements than was observed in past reports using FRET (Sohn et al., 2006, 2008b), possibly due to the different length-scales probed by these methods.
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work with speculation about the reason for the difference.

claim: Both PM enrichment and TM depletion extend beyond BCR clusters themselves.
source: We find that both PM enrichment and TM depletion extend beyond BCR clusters themselves (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the cross-correlation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The extended domain around BCR clusters likely arises from additional signaling structures assembled proximal to BCR.
source: It is likely that this extended domain arises from additional signaling structures assembled proximal to BCR, as is observed in other immune-receptor signaling systems (Balagopalan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculation based on comparison to other immune receptor systems, supported by citation.

claim: PM enrichment was reduced in cells treated with the Src kinase inhibitor PP2 prior to receptor clustering and fixation.
source: Further, PM enrichment was reduced in cells treated with the Src kinase inhibitor PP2 prior to receptor clustering and fixation (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), suggesting that ordered domain stabilization is amplified by receptor activation and the recruitment of down-stream signaling partners.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Ordered domain stabilization is amplified by receptor activation and the recruitment of down-stream signaling partners.
source: suggesting that ordered domain stabilization is amplified by receptor activation and the recruitment of down-stream signaling partners.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the PP2 inhibitor experiment.

claim: The same magnitude of PM and TM co-localization with BCR clusters was observed in live cells as in chemically fixed cells.
source: The same magnitude of PM and TM co-localization with BCR clusters was observed in live cells (Figure 2b) as in chemically fixed cells, indicating that co-localization is not an artifact of chemical fixation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing data from live and fixed cells in Figure 2.

claim: Co-localization of PM and TM with BCR clusters is not an artifact of chemical fixation.
source: indicating that co-localization is not an artifact of chemical fixation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing live and fixed cell data.

claim: PM proximal to BCR did not exhibit altered mobility in live cells.
source: We note that PM proximal to BCR did not exhibit altered mobility in live cells, indicating that PM enrichment arises from weak and/or transient interactions (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is demonstrated by step-size analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: PM enrichment around BCR arises from weak and/or transient interactions.
source: indicating that PM enrichment arises from weak and/or transient interactions (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the mobility data.

claim: Lyn proximal to BCR exhibits slowed diffusion, likely due to specific Lyn-BCR binding interactions.
source: As a counter-example, Lyn proximal to BCR does exhibit slowed diffusion, likely due to specific Lyn-BCR binding interactions.
evidence: This is demonstrated by step-size analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: PM was enriched within BCR clusters when CH27 cells were chemically fixed at 37°C.
source: PM was also enriched within BCR clusters when CH27 cells were chemically fixed at 37°C (Figure 2—figure supplement 8), indicating that ordered domains are formed at growth temperatures, although the magnitude of enrichment is reduced compared to the room temperature examples shown in Figure 2a.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 2—figure supplement 8.

claim: Ordered domains around BCR are formed at growth temperatures (37°C).
source: indicating that ordered domains are formed at growth temperatures
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 37°C fixation experiment.

claim: The magnitude of PM enrichment in BCR clusters is reduced at 37°C compared to room temperature.
source: although the magnitude of enrichment is reduced compared to the room temperature examples shown in Figure 2a.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of data at different temperatures.

claim: BCR clustering elicits a cellular response at both room temperature and 37°C.
source: We note that BCR clustering elicits a cellular response at both temperatures.
evidence: This is an observation from functional assays.

claim: Weak PM enrichment was observed around unclustered BCR in chemically fixed CH27 cells.
source: We additionally observed weak PM enrichment around unclustered BCR in chemically fixed CH27 cells, although the magnitude of this sorting is on the edge of the sensitivity limits of our imaging system (Figure 2—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 2—figure supplement 9.

claim: The magnitude of PM sorting with respect to unclustered BCR is comparable to the sorting of this peptide observed with respect to unclustered CTxB.
source: Interestingly, the magnitude of PM sorting with respect to unclustered BCR is comparable to the sorting of this peptide observed with respect to unclustered CTxB (Figure 2—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of cross-correlation data.

claim: CD45 and its minimal anchor peptide CD45TM were excluded from BCR clusters to the same extent.
source: Both CD45 and its minimal anchor peptide CD45TM were excluded from BCR clusters to the same extent, indicating that membrane domain interactions are sufficient to drive this partitioning.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 3a.

claim: Membrane domain interactions are sufficient to drive CD45 exclusion from BCR clusters.
source: indicating that membrane domain interactions are sufficient to drive this partitioning.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the equivalence of CD45 and CD45TM exclusion.

claim: Lyn kinase was more enriched in BCR clusters than its membrane anchor PM.
source: Lyn kinase was more enriched in BCR clusters than its membrane anchor PM, consistent with the direct binding of Lyn to phosphorylated ITAM sequences on BCR mediated by SH2 interaction domains in full-length Lyn (Johnson et al., 1995).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 3a and comparison to PM.

claim: The anchor sequence provides over one third of the energy associated with Lyn-BCR interactions.
source: PMFs between the BCR and PM or Lyn indicate that the anchor sequence provides over one third of the energy associated with Lyn-BCR interactions (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is calculated from the potential of mean force analysis shown in Figure 3b.

claim: BCR clusters are sites of tyrosine phosphorylation.
source: Both BCR and CTxB domains are sites of tyrosine phosphorylation (pY) as detected through a generic anti-pY antibody (4G10), while disordered TM domains were not enriched in pY proteins.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 3c.

claim: CTxB clusters are sites of tyrosine phosphorylation.
source: Both BCR and CTxB domains are sites of tyrosine phosphorylation (pY) as detected through a generic anti-pY antibody (4G10), while disordered TM domains were not enriched in pY proteins.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 3c.

claim: Disordered TM domains were not enriched in pY proteins.
source: while disordered TM domains were not enriched in pY proteins.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 3c.

claim: Activated Lyn (pY-397) was more enriched in CTxB clusters than Lyn as a whole.
source: Activated Lyn (pY-397) was more enriched in CTxB clusters than Lyn as a whole, indicating that ordered domains favor activation of this protein.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 3d.

claim: Ordered domains favor activation of Lyn.
source: indicating that ordered domains favor activation of this protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential enrichment of activated vs. total Lyn.

claim: CTxB clustering leads to Ca2+ mobilization.
source: In agreement with past reports (Francis et al., 1992), we found that CTxB clustering leads to Ca2+ mobilization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) without significantly altering the distribution of BCR (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: CTxB clustering does not significantly alter the distribution of BCR.
source: without significantly altering the distribution of BCR (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: CTxB binding and clustering resulted in subtle increases in tyrosine phosphorylation of multiple protein species detected within cellular extracts.
source: CTxB binding and clustering also resulted in subtle increases in tyrosine phosphorylation of multiple protein species detected within cellular extracts probed via Western blot (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blot data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Ordered domains contribute a substantial fraction of the free energy required to concentrate the kinase Lyn at BCR clusters.
source: We showed that ordered domains contribute a substantial fraction of the free energy required to concentrate the kinase Lyn and all of the free energy required to deplete the phosphatase CD45 from BCR clusters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the PMF analysis and comparison of full-length proteins to their anchors.

claim: Ordered domains contribute all of the free energy required to deplete the phosphatase CD45 from BCR clusters.
source: and all of the free energy required to deplete the phosphatase CD45 from BCR clusters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the equivalence of CD45 and CD45TM exclusion.

claim: Ordered domains provide a local environment that favors tyrosine phosphorylation.
source: Through this sorting, ordered domains provide a local environment that favors tyrosine phosphorylation, as supported by correlations between CTxB clusters and anti-pY antibodies even in the absence of specific recruitment of signaling machinery through protein-protein interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pY enrichment in CTxB clusters.

claim: A ~50% increase in the ratio of Lyn to CD45 due to sorting by ordered domains could cause a significant change in BCR phosphorylation levels.
source: It is reasonable to expect that the ~50% increase in the ratio of Lyn to CD45 due to sorting by ordered domains could cause a significant change in BCR phosphorylation levels if we compare to results obtained for the related T cell receptor (TCR) system.
evidence: This is a speculation based on comparison to the TCR system.

claim: In a reconstituted TCR system, TCR phosphorylation had switch-like dependence on the relative concentrations of Lck and CD45 at physiological levels.
source: In a reconstituted system, TCR phosphorylation was shown to have switch-like dependence on the relative concentrations of the Src kinase Lck, which is the analog of Lyn in the TCR system, and CD45 at physiological levels (Hui and Vale, 2014).
evidence: This is a citation to prior published work.

claim: The minimal model reproduced the sorting behavior of kinase and phosphatase anchor peptides observed experimentally.
source: Figure 4 describes a predictive model that reproduced the sorting behavior of kinase and phosphatase anchor peptides observed experimentally (Figure 4a and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing simulation results in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 to experimental data.

claim: Receptors became collectively activated upon clustering in simulations with a heterogeneous membrane and RBK feedback.
source: Through this set of minimal assumptions, receptors became collectively activated upon clustering (Figure 4b and Video 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results in Figure 4b.

claim: Clustered receptors were activated to a lesser extent in the absence of RBK positive feedback.
source: Clustered receptors were activated to a lesser extent in the absence of RBK positive feedback, but were not activated in a uniform membrane even with RBK feedback (Figure 4b and Videos 5 and 6).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results in Figure 4b.

claim: Clustered receptors were not activated in a uniform membrane even with RBK feedback.
source: but were not activated in a uniform membrane even with RBK feedback (Figure 4b and Videos 5 and 6).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results in Figure 4b.

claim: Receptor activation was observed when an ordered domain was stabilized using an external potential without confining receptors to the domain.
source: Receptor activation was also observed when an ordered domain was stabilized using an external potential without confining receptors to the domain (Figure 4c), mimicking the CTxB clustering result of Figure 3.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results in Figure 4c.

claim: The size of the ordered domain impacts the efficiency of receptor activation in simulations.
source: In these simulations, we also find that the size of the ordered domain impacts the efficiency of receptor activation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing simulations with different domain sizes in Figure 4c.

claim: The residency time of a receptor within the domain increases with increasing domain size.
source: This occurs because the residency time of a receptor within the domain increases with increasing domain size, as does the average number of receptors within the domain.
evidence: This is an explanation based on simulation observations.

claim: Phase-like heterogeneity is required for robust activation of BCR under simulation conditions.
source: Further, phase-like heterogeneity is required for robust activation of BCR under these simulation conditions.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing simulations with and without membrane heterogeneity in Figure 4b.

claim: Clustered receptors were more phosphorylated in simulations with a larger fraction of disordered components.
source: Clustered receptors were more phosphorylated in simulations with a larger fraction of disordered components and were less phosphorylated in simulations with more ordered components.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results in Figure 5a.

claim: Clustered receptors were less phosphorylated in simulations with more ordered components.
source: and were less phosphorylated in simulations with more ordered components.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results in Figure 5a.

claim: Varying the surface fraction of ordered vs. disordered components acts to enhance or suppress the local enrichment and depletion of signaling modulators at receptor clusters.
source: This occurs because varying the surface fraction of ordered vs. disordered components acts to enhance (or suppress) the local enrichment and depletion of signaling modulators at receptor clusters (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Acute modulation of cholesterol levels in intact cells with MβCD alters the surface fraction of coexisting ordered and disordered phases in GPMVs isolated from these cells.
source: Acute modulation of cholesterol levels in intact cells with methyl β cyclodextrin (MβCD) alters the surface fraction of coexisting ordered and disordered phases in GPMVs imaged at low temperature that were isolated from these cells (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is demonstrated by GPMV imaging data in Figure 5c.

claim: MβCD treatment does not affect cell viability as measured via annexin V binding to the extracellular surface.
source: This occurs without an effect on cell viability as measured via annexin V binding to the extracellular surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by annexin V binding assay in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Increased calcium mobilization upon BCR clustering was observed when cholesterol levels were acutely lowered with MβCD.
source: In intact B cells, we observed increased calcium mobilization upon BCR clustering when cholesterol levels were acutely lowered with MβCD, in agreement with past work (Awasthi-Kalia et al., 2001).
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging data in Figure 5c and supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Decreased calcium mobilization upon BCR clustering was observed in cells pretreated with MβCD-cholesterol complexes.
source: We also observed decreased calcium mobilization upon BCR clustering in cells pretreated with MβCD-cholesterol complexes, which act to increase cellular cholesterol levels (Christian et al., 1997).
evidence: This is demonstrated by calcium imaging data in Figure 5c and supported by citation.

claim: PM is more strongly enriched in BCR clusters in cells pretreated with MβCD than in untreated cells.
source: PM is more strongly enriched in BCR clusters in cells pretreated with MβCD than in untreated cells, and less strongly enriched in cells pretreated with MβCD-cholesterol complexes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 5d.

claim: PM is less strongly enriched in BCR clusters in cells pretreated with MβCD-cholesterol complexes than in untreated cells.
source: and less strongly enriched in cells pretreated with MβCD-cholesterol complexes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cross-correlation data in Figure 5d.

claim: The model is able to predict both the functional response associated with membrane perturbation and changes in domain-mediated sorting reported by super-resolution imaging experiments.
source: While the model clearly over-simplifies the behavior of the plasma membrane and the complexity of the BCR signaling pathway, it is able to predict both the functional response associated with membrane perturbation and changes in domain-mediated sorting reported by super-resolution imaging experiments.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing model predictions to experimental results in Figure 5.

claim: Modulating cholesterol levels using MβCD impacts the composition of the plasma membrane of B cells by varying the surface fraction of ordered vs. disordered components.
source: Therefore, we expect that modulating cholesterol levels using MβCD impacts the composition of the plasma membrane of B cells in a way that parallels the changes in our minimal model: by varying the surface fraction of ordered vs. disordered components.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the GPMV data and model predictions.

claim: Ordered and disordered domains were directly observed in cellular plasma membranes that resemble liquid-ordered and liquid-disordered phases in model membranes.
source: In conclusion, we directly observed domains in cellular plasma membranes that resemble liquid-ordered and liquid-disordered phases in model membranes.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Both enrichment and depletion of membrane species from phase-like domains in intact cells were visualized for the first time.
source: In these experiments we visualized both enrichment and, for the first time, depletion of membrane species from phase-like domains in intact cells.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the experimental observations.

claim: BCR clustering drove spatial co-localization or segregation of minimal membrane anchors from BCR clusters, consistent with the formation of an ordered phase-like domain.
source: BCR clustering drove spatial co-localization or segregation of minimal membrane anchors from BCR clusters, consistent with the formation of an ordered phase-like domain.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings in Figure 2.

claim: Ordered domains sorted BCR signaling partners into and out of receptor clusters.
source: These domains also sorted BCR signaling partners into and out of receptor clusters.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings in Figure 3.

claim: Formation of an ordered domain through protein clustering creates a local membrane environment that favors protein tyrosine phosphorylation.
source: Experiments that examined functional outcomes of BCR signaling indicated that formation of an ordered domain through protein clustering creates a local membrane environment that favors protein tyrosine phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pY enrichment data in Figure 3.

claim: Receptor clustering alone can initiate collective BCR activation by stabilizing an ordered membrane domain.
source: Based on these observations and supported by the predictive model, we propose a mechanism where receptor clustering alone can initiate collective BCR activation by stabilizing an ordered membrane domain.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on experimental and modeling results.

claim: Receptor clusters template a lipid domain in the membrane by stabilizing existing but very subtle and transient membrane composition fluctuations.
source: Instead, our findings support the idea that receptor clusters template a lipid domain in the membrane by stabilizing existing but very subtle and transient membrane composition fluctuations.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the experimental and modeling results.

claim: The effect of BCR clustering on downstream signaling depends on the size and stability of the resulting domain.
source: When BCR is clustered, the effect on downstream signaling depends on the size and stability of the resulting domain, which sets the level of access signaling partners have to resident BCR.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the simulation results showing domain size dependence.

claim: The structure of the BCR cluster and surrounding membrane can influence the activation state of individual BCRs.
source: As a consequence, the structure of the BCR cluster and surrounding membrane can influence the activation state of individual BCRs.
evidence: This is an inference from the collective nature of domain-mediated interactions.

claim: The entire cluster and associated domain, as opposed to single BCRs, comprise the basic signaling unit for the activation of B cells in this context.
source: Thus, the entire cluster and associated domain, as opposed to single BCRs, comprise the basic signaling unit for the activation of B cells in this context.
evidence: This is a conceptual conclusion about the nature of BCR signaling.

claim: Super-resolution microscopy is particularly well-suited to capture action-at-a-distance because it can measure interactions that span the length scale of the BCR cluster.
source: Super-resolution microscopy is particularly well-suited to capture this action-at-a-distance because it can measure interactions that span the length scale of the BCR cluster.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the experimental approach.

claim: Formation of phase-like domains through a collective ensemble of relatively weak protein-lipid and lipid-lipid interactions impacts overall signaling outcomes.
source: While BCR activation in vivo by natural antigens likely involves signal integration from multiple sources, our work suggests that formation of phase-like ordered domains through a collective ensemble of relatively weak protein-lipid and lipid-lipid interactions impacts overall signaling outcomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Lipid-mediated interactions can play a significant role in signal transduction from BCRs activated through protein clustering.
source: Thus, we both conclude that lipid-mediated interactions can play a significant role in signal transduction from BCRs activated through protein clustering and can describe a plausible mechanism for their action.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the work.

claim: The signaling function conferred by formation of phase-like domains around BCR clusters is an emergent property of a system where signaling molecules are compartmentalized based on their interactions with plasma membrane lipids.
source: We suggest that the signaling function conferred by formation of phase-like domains around BCR clusters is an emergent property of a system where signaling molecules are compartmentalized based on their interactions with plasma membrane lipids.
evidence: This is a conceptual interpretation of the results.

claim: Membrane domains are capable of contributing to a broad array of signal transduction pathways by altering the local concentration of regulatory proteins.
source: By extension, these findings suggest that membrane domains are capable of contributing to a broad array of signal transduction pathways by altering the local concentration of regulatory proteins, shifting the balance of biochemical networks.
evidence: This is a generalization of the findings to other signaling systems.

claim: CH27 cells are a mouse B cell lymphoma-derived cell line used as a model system for B lymphocyte signaling through the BCR.
source: CH27 cells (RRID: CVCL_7178), a mouse B cell lymphoma-derived cell line, was used as a model system for B lymphocyte signaling through the BCR (Haughton et al., 1986).
evidence: This is a description of the cell line used, supported by citation.

claim: The resolution of particle localization was close to 30 nm for all probes.
source: The resolution of particle localization was close to 30 nm for all probes, determined by correlation-based methods as detailed previously (Veatch et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a technical specification of the imaging system, supported by citation to methods.

claim: The cross-correlation analysis used has advantages over other co-clustering algorithms for images with low spatial sampling.
source: The cross-correlation analysis used here has advantages over other co-clustering algorithms for images with low spatial sampling, and can detect enrichment or depletion of probes even when this effect is not evident by visual inspection of images
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the analytical method used.

claim: The cross-correlation analysis can detect enrichment or depletion of probes even when this effect is not evident by visual inspection of images.
source: and can detect enrichment or depletion of probes even when this effect is not evident by visual inspection of images, as illustrated in Materials and methods.
evidence: This is demonstrated by examples in the Materials and methods section.

claim: In principle the cross-correlation analysis is insensitive to probe surface densities beyond an impact on signal to noise.
source: While in principle the cross-correlation analysis is insensitive to probe surface densities beyond an impact on signal to noise (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) (Veatch et al., 2012)
evidence: This is a theoretical property of the method, supported by simulations and citation.
